rule: RS-15. Each entry is one limit the syllabus states, or one A Level section the AS route excludes, with the pattern C-11 scans learner-facing text for. The sentence is the syllabus’s; the pattern is our judgement of what teaching past the limit would look like. Every contract in the subject carries every entry.

must_catch: Memorise the ASCII codes for the capital letters.
You should remember the ASCII code values for A to Z.
must_allow: Given that the ASCII code for A is 65, the code for C is 67.
ASCII uses 7 bits per character.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Students will not be expected to memorise any particular character codes.

entries.construct: a logic gate with more than two inputs

must_allow: The circuit has three inputs, A, B and C.
Each AND gate has two inputs.

entries.syllabus_sentence: All gates except the NOT gate will have two inputs only.

entries.construct: more than one general purpose register

must_catch: Load the value into a second general purpose register.
must_allow: The accumulator is the only general purpose register.
The index register (IX) is a special purpose register.

entries.syllabus_sentence: All questions will assume there is only one general purpose register available (Accumulator)

entries.construct: writing pseudocode to implement a stack, queue or linked list

must_catch: Write pseudocode to implement a stack using an array.
Write the pseudocode for a queue.
must_allow: Complete the pseudocode for the function Push().
Describe how a stack can be implemented using an array.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Candidates will not be required to write pseudocode for these structures, but they should be able to add, edit and delete data from these structures

entries.construct: program code in a programming language on Paper 2

must_allow: OUTPUT "Hello"
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
FUNCTION Total(A : INTEGER, B : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER

entries.syllabus_sentence: Candidates will not be required to write programming code.

must_allow: REAL is a data type for numbers with a fractional part.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 13.3 Floating-point numbers, representation and manipulation.

entries.construct: file organisation and access methods (A Level 13.2)
entries.pattern: \b(?:random|direct)[- ]access files?\b|\bhashing algorithm\b|\bsequential file organisation\b|\bserial file organisation\b

must_catch: a hashing algorithm finds the record
must_allow: A text file is read one line at a time from the start.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 13.2 File organisation and access.

must_allow: The start pointer holds the index of the first node.
A record is a user-defined structure.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 13.1 User-defined data types.

must_allow: Data is sent across the internet in packets.
A router forwards packets.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 14.1 Protocols; 14.2 Circuit switching, packet switching.

entries.construct: processor design, parallel processing and virtual machines (A Level 15.1)

must_allow: A virtual reality headset has two displays.
The processor has four cores.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 15.1 Processors, Parallel Processing and Virtual Machines.

entries.construct: Boolean algebra, De Morgan and Karnaugh maps (A Level 15.2)

must_allow: Construct the truth table for the logic expression.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 15.2 Boolean Algebra and Logic Circuits.

entries.construct: encryption protocols and digital certificates (A Level 17)

must_allow: Encryption makes intercepted data impossible to understand without the key.
A digital signature authenticates the sender.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 17.1 Encryption, Encryption Protocols and Digital Certificates.

must_allow: AI can be used to answer customer questions.

entries.construct: algorithms and recursion beyond AS (A Level 19)

must_allow: A linear search checks each element in turn.
A bubble sort compares adjacent elements.

must_allow: A procedure is called as a statement.

entries.syllabus_sentence: A Level content: 20.1 Programming Paradigms; 20.2 File Processing and Exception Handling.
